cited_evidence: top_level_input includes n06-r01 with demand_score 9, record_id n06-r01, need 'isolate faulty execution branches before replay'.
select_demand source selects records where demand_score >= 3 or fallback ids; selected_df and selected output artifacts each have 8 rows.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r09','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r06','n06-r07','n06-r08'], omitting n06-r01.
normalize retained_df and final needs_df artifacts have 7 rows, and the job_2 input needs list contains n06-r02 through n06-r08 only.
handoff-needs records identical producer_sha256 and consumer_sha256, showing job_2 received the upstream needs artifact exactly.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution is faulty because the upstream job selected all 8 qualifying corpus records, including n06-r01 with demand_score 9, but the upstream normalize function filtered against an allowed_record_ids list that omits n06-r01 and instead includes n06-r09. This reduced the needs handoff to 7 rows and silently removed the highest-demand stipulated record before the exact handoff to job_2. The downstream job consumed that exact 7-row handoff and ranked it consistently, so the supported localization is upstream normalize.
